question.text: In reviewing past performance track records in a DDQ, the data an institutional LP will typically demand includes BOTH portfolio-level IRR and investor-level IRR. The DIFFERENCE between these two is:

answer.text: Portfolio-level IRR includes taxes; investor-level IRR excludes taxes.

Portfolio-level IRR is gross AND net of all fees/expenses/carry at the fund deal portfolio level, while investor-level IRR (post fee and carry) is computed based on actual drawdowns and distributions to the investors.
Portfolio-level IRR is for listed investments only; investor-level IRR is for unlisted.
They are identical in all fund structures.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Annexure 12.1, the DDQ asks for both 'Portfolio level IRR, both gross and net (post all fees, expenses and carry)' and 'Investor level IRR (post fee and carry) - based on drawdowns and distribution to the investors'. Chapter 9 also supports the gross/net IRR distinction. The investor-level number uses the timing of actual capital calls and distributions, which differs from the portfolio-level view. The Trap: Tax treatment, listed-vs-unlisted scope, and the claim that the two IRRs are identical in all structures are distinctions the workbook does not make. Note: The portfolio-level metric measures performance at the deal portfolio; the investor-level metric reflects what the LP actually realises after drawdowns, distributions, fees and carry.
